# aitmproxy MCP tool reference

<!-- GENERATED FILE — do not edit by hand. -->
<!-- Regenerate: `node aitmproxy-plugin/scripts/gen-tool-reference.mjs` -->

This reference is generated by `aitmproxy-plugin/scripts/gen-tool-reference.mjs`
from the command listing the `aitm` binary prints on its usage error
(`target/debug/aitm --help`; `--help` is not a real flag, the CLI answers
`expected a command before flags` and lists every command with its parameters on
stderr). It was last regenerated from a build of `main` at 1b79813 run with
`AITM_CONFIG` pointing at a config that sets `l4.enabled: true`, so the `l4.*`
family is listed below; the same core's live `tools/list` carried the same 113
names. The raw listing is kept in `docs/research/mcp-tool-catalog.txt`.

Tool names are shown in dot form (`flow.list`), as the MCP server exposes them;
the one-shot `aitm` CLI accepts the same commands space-separated
(`aitm flow list`). The Parameters column uses the CLI spelling (`--id <flow-id>`,
`[--mode <string>]` optional); over MCP the same names are the keys of the tool's
JSON arguments, e.g. `{ "id": "<flow-id>" }`. Note that the one-shot CLI runs its own
in-process core and cannot steer a running proxy; drive a live proxy over MCP or
from the web UI, the TUI or the macOS app.

**113 tools across 25 namespaces.** The 22 `l4.*` module verbs (the `l4.agent`,
`l4.capture`, `l4.flow`, `l4.intercept` and `l4.scope` namespaces plus
`l4.interfaces`, `l4.craft`, `l4.inject` and `l4.send_recv`) are registered only
when `config.yaml` sets `l4.enabled: true`; without it a core lists 91 tools, and
the only `l4.*` names left are the three bundled Rhai scripts (`l4.recon`,
`l4.tcp_probe`, `l4.udp_probe`), which need the module to do anything. What to
know about the family:

- Capture, inject and send/recv need raw-socket privilege (read+write
  `/dev/bpf*` on macOS, `CAP_NET_RAW` on Linux). The in-path `l4.intercept.*`
  verbs (`start`, `stop`, `list`, `mutate`, `revert`, `forward`, `drop`) are
  Linux NFQUEUE only: they need `CAP_NET_ADMIN` and an `l4.intercept` config
  block, and report `unsupported_platform` on macOS.
- `l4.capture.status` and `l4.intercept.status` always answer, never with
  `L4 unavailable`, as `{available, code, reason, …}`: `available` is a bool,
  `code` is one of `available`, `needs_privilege`, `unsupported_platform` or
  `not_configured`, `reason` is the text the gated verbs would return after
  `L4 unavailable: ` (null when available), and the payload (`captures` /
  `sessions`) is `[]` when unavailable.
- `l4.flow.get` takes `offset` (default 0) and `limit` (default 256, clamped to
  4096; `limit: 0` returns the flow fields with `packets: []`); `packet_count`
  is always the total, and when the 4 MiB raw-byte budget stops the window
  early the reply carries `truncated: true` and `next_offset`. Each packet
  carries `bytes` (padded base64) for the operator and the CLI always; for an
  agent (MCP) the decision is per packet: a captured packet (`injected: false`)
  carries `bytes` only while the agent's Capture gate is open, an authored
  packet (`injected: true`) only while its Inject gate is open. A packet the
  caller may not read keeps every other field and simply has no `bytes` key.
- `l4.scope.add` from an agent is refused (`runtime L4 scope widening is
  disabled; declare scope in the l4.scope config …`) unless the Widen gate
  (`l4.agent.set --capability widen --allowed true`) is open. The operator and
  the CLI are not Widen-gated: `l4.scope.add` is confirmable (`confirmable:
  true` in `tools/list`); an operator call answers `needs_confirmation` with a
  prompt summarising the entry (cidr, ports or `all ports`, interface,
  direction, capability, inject rate or `inject refused (rate 0)`, and a
  `WARNING` for a prefix wider than /16 (IPv4) or /48 (IPv6)) and proceeds
  when re-issued with `_confirm`; the CLI asks its confirmer unless `--yes`.
  The entry is stored with `source: runtime` and never lifts the
  dangerous-destination denylist; only `config.yaml` entries can.

## `flow.*`

| Tool | Parameters | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `flow.list` | — | List the ids of every captured flow, oldest first. |
| `flow.get` | `--id <flow-id>` | Summarize one captured flow: kind, request line, status, state. The summary carries the five per-host decryption keys with the same names and values as a `flow.table` row and the `flow.subscribe` push summary: `tunnel` (`decrypted` \| `passthrough` \| `failed`; null when the flow is not a CONNECT tunnel row), `tunnel_reason` (passthrough: `out_of_scope` \| `pinned`; failed: `client_rejected_certificate` \| `client_closed` \| `client_tls_error` \| `upstream_unreachable` \| `upstream_tls_failed` \| `protocol_error`; else null), `bytes_up` / `bytes_down` (int, set when a passthrough tunnel closes; else null) and `passive` (bool, always present: plain HTTP to a host outside Scope, observed but nothing acted on it). |
| `flow.table` | — | Per-flow summaries for a flows table: method, URL, status, duration, state, and marks, oldest first. Read-only. Every CONNECT is a row, and each row carries `tunnel`: `decrypted` (TLS terminated with the proxy's leaf; the inner requests are their own rows), `passthrough` (relayed byte for byte, the client saw the origin's certificate) or `failed` (never established), null for a flow that is not a tunnel row; `tunnel_reason`: `out_of_scope` \| `pinned` for a passthrough, `client_rejected_certificate` \| `client_closed` \| `client_tls_error` \| `upstream_unreachable` \| `upstream_tls_failed` \| `protocol_error` for a failure, else null. A tunnel relays TLS only: a CONNECT whose first byte inside the tunnel is not a TLS record is refused and recorded as `failed` with `tunnel_reason` `protocol_error`; `bytes_up` / `bytes_down`: bytes a passthrough tunnel relayed, set when it closes, else null; `passive` (bool, always present): true for plain HTTP to a host outside Scope — observed only, no breakpoint rule, script or map rule touched it; false for every tunnel row. A tunnel row's `status` is 200 once established and null when it failed; its `duration_ms` is null while the tunnel is open. |
| `flow.subscribe` | `[--filter <json-object>] [--since <flow-id>]` | Subscribe to live flow notifications on this connection. Returns a sub_id; matching flows then arrive as notifications/aitm/flow lines with no further request. Read-only. |
| `flow.unsubscribe` | `--sub_id <int>` | Cancel a flow subscription on this connection. Read-only. |
| `flow.detail` | `--id <flow-id> [--body <string>] [--offset <int>] [--length <int>]` | Full detail for one flow: headers, bodies, connection info, timing and edit state. `body` selects none\|inline\|range (default inline). `meta` adds `passive` (bool) and `tunnel`: an object `{mode, reason, bytes_up, bytes_down}` for a CONNECT tunnel row (`mode` is `decrypted` \| `passthrough` \| `failed`; `reason` and the byte counts take the same values as `flow.table`'s `tunnel_reason` / `bytes_up` / `bytes_down`), or null when the flow is not a tunnel row. |
| `flow.mark` | `--id <flow-id> --marks <json-array>` | Replace a flow's highlight mark set (e.g. colour names); an empty array clears it. |
| `flow.comment` | `--id <flow-id> --text <string>` | Set a flow's free-text comment; an empty string clears it. |
| `flow.replay` | `--id <flow-id>` | Reissue a captured HTTP request through the proxy client; returns the new flow's id. |
| `flow.intercept` | `[--enabled <true\|false>] [--rules <json-array>]` | Arm (default) or disarm interception. With no rules every request is parked (global arm); with rules only a request matching a rule at its phase is parked. A parked flow waits for flow.resume or flow.kill. |
| `flow.resume` | `--id <flow-id>` | Release an intercepted flow so its (possibly mutated) request is forwarded. |
| `flow.kill` | `--id <flow-id> [--mode <string>]` | Abort an intercepted flow. mode=reset (default) drops it so the client sees a reset/closed connection; mode=429 or mode=503 answers the client with that status and an empty body, with no upstream request. |
| `flow.clear` | — | Remove completed flows from the store (in-flight and intercepted flows are kept); returns {cleared, skipped_in_flight}. |
| `flow.mutate` | `--id <flow-id> --edits <json-object>` | Edit a captured HTTP flow in place. Edits apply to the request (method, path, headers, body); when the flow is parked at the response phase they apply to the response and `status` is valid. |
| `flow.export` | `[--ids <json-array>] [--format <string>] [--path <string>]` | Export selected flows (or the whole store) as `aitm` native JSON or HAR 1.2. Returns bytes, or writes to `path` when given. |
| `flow.import` | `[--path <string>] [--bytes <text>] [--format <string>]` | Import flows (by `path` or `bytes`) into the store, marked `imported`. Formats: `aitm`, `har`, or mitmproxy `.flows`. Passive: no upstream requests, never replays. |

## `proxy.*`

| Tool | Parameters | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `proxy.status` | — | The proxy's live state: `listening` (bool) + `address`, `intercept_armed`, `paused` (parked-flow count), `capturing`, `flows` (visible count), `version` (the aitm binary's version), and `system_proxy` (the OS proxy setting as this core sees it: `state` one of points_at_us/other/off/unknown/unsupported, `host`/`port` when `other`, `managed_by_us`, `setting`, `supported`, `detail`; refreshed at most every 5 s), and `decrypt` (`scope_hosts`: entries in Scope, the decryption list; `decrypting`: scope_hosts > 0; `advice`: the one sentence to show when nothing is decrypted, else null). With an empty Scope `advice` is exactly `Nothing is decrypted until a host is in Scope.`; frontends print it verbatim and never compose their own. |
| `proxy.pause` | — | Pause capture: new flows are hidden from list/status/count. Traffic still flows and each hidden flow stays in memory, reachable by id, until it ages out via normal eviction (use flow.clear to drop completed ones). While paused, continued traffic can evict older visible flows under the store's capacity bound, so resume or clear to reclaim history. Returns the capture state. |
| `proxy.resume` | — | Resume capture: new flows are shown again. Returns the capture state. |

| Tool | Parameters | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `scope.add` | `--host <string>` | Add a host, host:port, or *.wildcard to Scope. New connections to it are decrypted from now on; hosts outside Scope are tunnelled. Refused from an agent frontend (MCP) unless scope.allow_agent_widen is set. |

## `ca.*`

| Tool | Parameters | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ca.export` | `[--format <string>] [--out <string>]` | Export the aitmproxy root CA certificate (never its key) as PEM or DER, with its SHA-256 and SHA-1 fingerprints and the CA directory. Always available. This is for TLS clients you bring yourself; the embedded obscura browser already trusts the CA through --ca-cert and needs no export. |
| `ca.status` | — | Report the aitmproxy root CA: whether ca.crt exists, its fingerprints and path, and, per trust-store scope on this platform, whether a certificate with its fingerprint is installed and trusted. Read-only, always available, not audited. The embedded obscura browser does not use the OS store (it trusts the CA through --ca-cert), so these fields say nothing about it. |
| `ca.install` | `[--scope <string>] [--dry_run <true\|false>]` | Install the aitmproxy root CA into the OS trust store (macOS keychain via `security`, Linux ca-certificates anchors, Windows Root store via certutil); every TLS client that uses that store will then trust certificates this proxy mints. Idempotent; identifies the certificate by fingerprint; never reads the CA key. Refused from an agent frontend (MCP) unless ca.allow_agent_install is set in the aitmproxy config; dry_run is always allowed and lists the commands that would run. The embedded obscura browser does not use the OS store (it trusts the CA through --ca-cert) and is unaffected. |
| `ca.uninstall` | `[--scope <string>] [--dry_run <true\|false>]` | Remove the aitmproxy root CA from the OS trust store (macOS keychain via `security`, Linux ca-certificates anchors, Windows Root store via certutil); TLS clients that use that store stop trusting certificates this proxy mints. Idempotent; identifies the certificate by fingerprint; never reads the CA key. Refused from an agent frontend (MCP) unless ca.allow_agent_install is set in the aitmproxy config; dry_run is always allowed and lists the commands that would run. The embedded obscura browser does not use the OS store (it trusts the CA through --ca-cert) and is unaffected. |

## `agent.*`

| Tool | Parameters | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `agent.status` | `[--exclude_self <true\|false>]` | Report the current agent policy and recent agent activity. Read-only and readable by any role, but the activity count covers only the entries the caller may see: a caller that is not trusted control does not count entries made by trusted control (operator, CLI). |
| `agent.set` | `--policy <string>` | Set the agent policy (all \| auto \| ask \| readonly \| paused). The deliberate operator act that governs the agent — operator/CLI only; the agent cannot change its own policy. |
| `agent.activity` | `[--since <int>] [--limit <int>]` | Recent command-invocation audit entries (who ran what, with what redacted arguments, and the outcome), oldest first. A live view, not a complete record: a high-volume source can flush other sources' entries. `origin` is authoritative; `client_label` is an unauthenticated display string. A call with no `limit` can return at most 6144 entries at the default sizes, so pass `limit`. Read-only and readable by any role, but a caller that is not trusted control does not see entries made by trusted control (operator, CLI). |
| `agent.approve` | `--request_id <string> --allow <true\|false>` | Approve or deny a Sensitive agent command the server parked under the `ask` policy. Operator/CLI only; the agent cannot approve its own requests. |

## `script.*`

| Tool | Parameters | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `script.validate` | `[--path <string>] [--source <string>]` | Compile a .rhai script without loading it; reports its name, API, hooks and the commands/options its load(reg) registers (a static scan; empty when the names are not literals), or the positioned compile error. Give exactly one of `path` (a file) or `source` (the script text, compiled in the sandbox with nothing written). |
| `script.reload` | `--name <string>` | Recompile a loaded script from its file and swap its hooks live; a failed recompile keeps the previous version. Commands and options it registered at load are unchanged until restart. |
| `script.findings` | `[--limit <int>]` | Findings scripts emitted with finding(...) this run (in-memory, not persisted): each as an object, oldest first, plus how many the bounded sink dropped. For the persistent store use findings.list/get/record. |
| `script.list` | — | List the loaded scripts in chain order: name, path, API, hooks, whether enabled, and the most recent hook error (null if none). |
| `script.enable` | `--name <string>` | Turn a loaded script's hooks back on live. Idempotent. Answers { name, enabled }. |
| `script.disable` | `--name <string>` | Turn a loaded script's hooks off live without unloading it; commands and options it registered stay (the registry is sealed). Idempotent. Answers { name, enabled }. |
| `script.save` | `--name <string> --source <string> [--enable <true\|false>]` | Write a script to <scripts_dir>/<name>.rhai after checking it compiles (a non-compiling source writes nothing). Its hooks go live immediately with no restart — for a brand-new name (appended to the running script host) as well as a save over a loaded script (swapped live). restart_required is true ONLY when the script registers commands or options, which the sealed registry cannot add until a restart; its hooks still run this session. Answers { name, path, api, hooks, registers, restart_required }. Needs rhai.scripts_dir. |

## `tls.passthrough.*`

| Tool | Parameters | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tls.passthrough.list` | — | List the hosts whose TLS is tunnelled (not decrypted). Pins win over Scope: a pinned host is tunnelled even when it is in Scope (its CONNECT row has `tunnel` `passthrough`, `tunnel_reason` `pinned`). |
| `tls.passthrough.add` | `--host <string>` | Add a host or *.wildcard to the TLS passthrough list (tunnel, do not decrypt). Refused from an agent frontend (MCP) unless tls.allow_agent_passthrough is set. A pin wins over Scope: the host stays tunnelled (`tunnel_reason` `pinned`) even while it is in Scope. |
| `tls.passthrough.remove` | `--host <string>` | Remove an entry from the TLS passthrough list. Refused from an agent frontend (MCP) unless tls.allow_agent_passthrough is set. Removing a pin does not by itself decrypt the host: new connections to it are decrypted only if it is also in Scope. |

## `capture.*`

| Tool | Parameters | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `capture.status` | — | What the core knows about the macOS Network/System Extension capture path: whether `macos_capture.enabled` is set, whether the capture feeder is listening, whether a code-signature-verified extension provider is attached, the scope it holds, and the flows it has handed off during the current attachment. Read-only and parameterless. Times are Unix epoch milliseconds. When `feeder.state` is `off`, `feeder.reason` is exactly one of `macos_capture.enabled is false`, `not a macOS build`, `not started`, `stopped`. This is not the record toggle: `proxy.status.capturing` reports whether the proxy records flows. |

| `l4.send_recv` | `--spec <value> --dst <string> --interface <string> [--port <int>] [--timeout_ms <int>] [--expect <string>]` | Scapy sr/sr1: inject a crafted stimulus and return the correlated reply (Response / Other / NoResponse) linked to the stimulus in an L4 flow. Guarded (Inject+Capture); never hangs (bounded by `timeout_ms`). |

| Tool | Parameters | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `l4.flow.list` | — | List the ids of every captured / crafted / send-recv / intercepted L4 flow, oldest first (read-only). |
| `l4.flow.get` | `--id <string> [--offset <int>] [--limit <int>]` | Summarize one L4 flow: kind, bind, creation time, endpoints, and a window of its packets with bytes, time and addresses (read-only). `packet_count` is always the total; list polling should pass `limit: 0` and let only an inspector fetch a window. A reply carries at most 4 MiB of raw packet bytes; when that stops the window early, `truncated` is true and `next_offset` is where to resume. |

## `l4.intercept.*`

| Tool | Parameters | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `l4.intercept.start` | `--interface <string> [--direction <string>] [--queue_num <int>]` | Bind the in-path NFQUEUE and open a guarded interception session (Linux). Requires an `Intercept` scope entry on the interface + direction; returns the session's flow id. `L4Unavailable` when in-path is disabled or unsupported. |
| `l4.intercept.stop` | `--flow <string>` | End an interception session by flow id; fail-open forwards anything still parked. `false` if no such session. |
| `l4.intercept.list` | `[--flow <string>]` | List the packets currently parked awaiting a verdict, across sessions or for one `flow` (read-only), in arrival order, oldest first. |
| `l4.intercept.mutate` | `--id <string> [--spec <value>] [--bytes <text>]` | Edit a parked packet via a PacketSpec (`spec`) or raw `bytes`, keeping the original as a backup for `l4.intercept.revert`. The edit is reinjected only when the packet is forwarded. |
| `l4.intercept.revert` | `--id <string>` | Discard a staged mutation on a parked packet, restoring its original bytes. `false` if nothing was staged. |
| `l4.intercept.forward` | `--id <string>` | Forward a parked packet through the guarded verdict path — mangled if it was mutated, otherwise the kernel's original. `false` if the id is not parked. |
| `l4.intercept.drop` | `--id <string>` | Drop a parked packet (verdict Drop). `false` if the id is not parked. |
| `l4.intercept.status` | — | Report whether in-path interception is available on this core (`available`, `code`, `reason`) and the live interception sessions with their parked-packet counts. Always answers, never `L4 unavailable`. |

## `l4.scope.*`

| Tool | Parameters | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `l4.scope.add` | `--cidr <string> --interface <string> --direction <string> --capability <string> [--ports <string>] [--inject_rate_pps <int>] [--inject_rate_burst <int>]` | Add an entry to the deny-by-default L4 scope (CIDR, ports, interface, direction, capability, injection rate). The single escape hatch that brings a target into play. |
| `l4.scope.remove` | `--id <string>` | Remove an L4 scope entry by id (reverts that target to deny-by-default). |
| `l4.scope.list` | — | List the current L4 scope entries (read-only). |

## `proxy.system.*`

| Tool | Parameters | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `proxy.system.status` | — | Read the OS system proxy: where it points relative to this core, whether this core manages it, and the per-service rows on macOS. |
| `proxy.system.set` | `[--bypass <json-array>]` | Point the OS system proxy (HTTP and HTTPS) at this core, recording the previous setting so it is restored on unset or exit. Operator-only. |
| `proxy.system.unset` | — | Restore the OS system proxy this core set, service by service, from the recorded previous setting; services another tool changed since are left alone. Operator-only. |

## `scan.*`

| Tool | Parameters | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `scan.discover` | `--target <string> [--max_depth <int>] [--max_pages <int>]` | Discover reachable in-scope URLs under `target` (same-origin, scope-bound, budget-capped) and enumerate the injection points visible in captured requests. No injection or fuzzing is performed. `max_depth`/`max_pages` may lower the configured caps, never raise them. A navigation that lands off-origin or out of scope (a redirect) aborts the crawl with `stopped_reason = "left_scope"`. While the crawl runs the proxy's browser-egress posture is held confined, so the embedded browser cannot fetch an out-of-scope public host (sub-resource or redirect target); the hold is released when the command returns. Only one discovery runs at a time (crawls share one browser page); a second call while one is running is refused immediately — wait for it to finish. Needs the embedded browser for a real crawl; see `docs/scanner.md`. |
| `scan.passive` | `[--target <string>]` | Run the passive checks (reflected request parameters, missing security headers, cookie flags) over the flows already captured for `target`, or over every captured flow when `target` is absent. Issues no traffic. Findings carry the parameter, header or cookie NAME, never its value. |
| `scan.report` | `[--target <string>]` | Fold the recorded findings into `report_md` (one markdown section per finding) and `index` (one {poc_path, target_path, class, passed, control_passed, finding_capture, screenshot_path} entry per finding). `target` selects the findings recorded against that origin, or against a path under it. Empty when no findings directory is configured. Credentials are masked. |
